# Pending changes (since patch 0029, 2026-11-28)

## 2026-11-28 - The automaton's rifle: a detailed folding mechanism and a compartment in the hip

**Asked:** make the automaton's rifle much more detailed, and give it a real mechanical fold - panels, barrel,
stock, sights and grip sliding, rotating and telescoping into each other piece after piece until it is a compact
block (and the reverse, ending snapped into shape in the hands). When it's put away, an armoured compartment on the
hip/thigh opens, the folded rifle goes in, the lid shuts; drawing it, the lid opens, the folded rifle comes out into
the hand and unfolds as it rises. And the user's own mesh-editor override of the automaton (whose rifle is the old
one) must show the new rifle and compartment too.

**Done:**
- **The rifle** (external/blender/automaton/automaton.py `rifle()`): rebuilt of some 70 parts on 14 bones - the receiver
  (panel seams, ejection port and cover, charging handle, a toothed rail, status lights, screws, armoured lower
  plates, magazine well), a grip with rubber panels and a trigger and guard, a magazine with a glowing ammo window,
  a rear receiver sleeve with the stock's hinge, a skeleton stock (two struts, a web, a cheek rest with a red mark)
  and a telescoping butt pad on rods, a fore-end sleeve with vents, heat fins, a cap and two hinged side panels with
  light strips, a barrel with a shroud and cooling rings, a squared muzzle brake with ports, a scope with an eyecup,
  turret, knob and a telescoping front. PBR materials by name as before (AUT_Gun / AUT_Armor / AUT_GunOrange /
  AUT_Grey / AUT_Joint / AUT_Glow...).
- **The fold** (`GUN_FOLD`, now a list of timed moves per piece - kit._moves: slides summed, turns in turn, each in
  its own share of "fold" 0..1): the muzzle brake twists a quarter turn free (0-0.08), the fore-end's side panels
  swing out 70 deg (0.04-0.14), the barrel telescopes 0.255 m into the fore-end (0.10-0.28), the fore-end slides
  0.24 m back over the receiver (0.24-0.42), the panels lock again (0.40-0.48), the scope's front telescopes in
  (0.44-0.52), the scope lifts off its rail, swings a quarter turn down its left side about a hinge inside the
  receiver and seats (0.48-0.70), the fore-grip slides up into the lower (0.56-0.64), the magazine slides up into
  its well (0.60-0.70), the butt pad telescopes in (0.62-0.70), the stock swings 180 deg forward along the right
  side (0.70-0.86), the rear receiver telescopes forward (0.84-0.92), the grip folds flat under it (0.92-1.0).
  1.13 m long -> a 0.36 x 0.23 x 0.16 m block. Unfolding is the same in reverse: the brake's turn last - the snap.
- **The hip compartment** (`holster()`, `POD`; kit.POD - new bones `holster.R` (on thigh.R) and `holster.R.lid`, a
  new pose control "lid" 0 shut .. 1 open): a box down the outside of the right thigh (armoured walls, grey linings,
  clamps, rims, a red latch, a light, hinge knuckles, two bands and brackets round the thigh) laid round the folded
  rifle (moves.HOLSTER: grip at the box's top, muzzle down, its top toward the thigh), and its lid - cream armour,
  chamfered, a red band and the automaton's triangle (a flat plate), vents, a light strip, a catch - hinged along
  the front outer edge: unlatched outward 6 mm, then swung 115 deg out and forward. Checked by script: the folded
  rifle sits wholly inside the box (no vertex out), no thigh vertex inside it, the block leaves the box clear of its
  walls.
- **Draw / holster** (moves.draw_clips, 32 frames each = 1.07 s; played at DRAW_SPEED 1.1 -> ~0.95 s): leaning to the
  right (bend 20 deg) the hand reaches down as the lid unlatches and swings open (frames 1-8), the folded grip
  springs out to meet it (4-8), the block is drawn straight out of the box (9-13; the hand on it within 3 cm), the
  lid shuts behind it (12-19), and it rises and swings forward unfolding piece by piece (13-29), the left hand meeting
  the fore-grip; put away the other way (folding 2-17, the lid open 12-18, in at 22, the grip folding in as the hand
  lets go 23-27, the lid shut 25-32). Fold and lid are per-frame tracks (moves._track), the pieces ease themselves.
- **ArmsLayer** (scripts/world/player/arms_layer.gd): poses every "gun.*" and "holster.*" bone the skeleton has (not a
  fixed list); while the clip has the rifle in or by its box it rides the legs' thigh, not the clip's (_in_box) - so
  drawing while walking the block stays in the opening box. MUZZLE (0, 0.785, 0.08).
- **The user's override** (scripts/world/models/model_override.gd `_graft`, from `_with_base_clips`): an override's
  rifle and hip compartment always come from the game's model (GRAFT: "gun", "gun.*", "holster.*" by bone name) - the
  bones it lacks added under the same parents with the model's rests, its own parts on those bones taken out (a
  part all on them removed; partly on them, the rest kept), the model's parts on them added as one skinned mesh
  "Grafted" with the Body's skin (the binds it lacks added) - so CosmosModels still merges the character into one
  surface. Only for a model with the hip compartment (the automaton - not the pirate's rifle edits), and not when
  the original itself is read at run time. The user's override files are untouched. Their variant 1: 15 bones added (21 -> 36), its 5 old rifle
  parts ("Gun", "Gun Armor", "Gun Orange", "Gun Grey", "Gun Glow") replaced; built in ~0.2 s (on a worker, as before).
- Reloaded live into the running game (the walker re-dressed: the model's caches forgotten, the new model put on).

**Numbers:** the player model 28,390 -> 35,654 triangles in model.json (the generated rifle 4,780 + compartment 2,040
triangles in Blender; the export's zero-thickness ink copy - dropped at the merge - doubles them in the glb); bones
25 -> 36 (new: gun.grip, gun.mag, gun.rear, gun.stockpad, gun.foregrip, gun.panel.L, gun.panel.R, gun.muzzle,
gun.lens, holster.R, holster.R.lid); 49 clips (none added or renamed); draw / holster 18 -> 32 frames.

**Names:** none renamed or removed - every old bone (gun, gun.stock, gun.fore, gun.barrel, gun.scope), part and
material name kept; new ones added. GUN_HAND_L moved 3 cm back (0.255 -> 0.225) with the fore-grip. The old
"Holster" part's pieces are now on the holster.R bone (still part names "Holster...").

**Files:** external/blender/automaton/kit.py (_moves, fold_moves, POD, "lid"), automaton.py (rifle, GUN_FOLD,
holster, POD), moves.py (HOLSTER, draw_clips, _track), build.py (kit.POD, the muzzle point); art/player_3d/player.glb
+ model.json (re-exported); scripts/world/player/arms_layer.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd (DRAW_SPEED

the lid opening, the draw waited for by time), tests/test_overrides.gd (test_override_gets_the_models_rifle_and_hip_box). Doc shots retaken: space3d_foot,
space3d_hangar, space3d_climb, space3d_dig.

## 2026-11-28 - The mushroom mammoth: its own detailed model and motion; towering and calm

**Asked:** make the mushroom mammoth (CosmosFauna "mykelephas", drawn till now by the generic "heavy" kit) far more
detailed and realistic, with realistic animation - following the red fox's pattern. Then (two additions): it must not
run from you - calm, grazing and walking its own way as you come - and be at least six times larger, a towering beast
(with everything that follows from its size: collisions, reach, health, distance drawing, spawning, step length and
speed, the camera, the tests), shown next to the automaton for scale.

**Done:**
- **CosmosMammoth** (scripts/world/life/cosmos_mammoth.gd, like CosmosFox): one shared skinned mesh made on a worker
  (one surface, one draw call, 6 LOD levels made by meshoptimizer through ImporterMesh) over a 31-bone rig each mammoth
  builds. The model: a massive body (a high domed shoulder, the back sloping to a rounded rump, a heavy hanging belly -
  a superellipse section through Catmull-Rom keys), a short folded neck, a big domed skull, small deep-set eyes in
  wrinkled lids, a pink lower lip on a chewing jaw, large fan ears (two bones each: the fan rolls out to the edge, a
  ragged cupped edge), a 21-ring trunk on six bones ending in a finger, curved tusks (out, down and forward, then up
  and in) in skin sheaths, pillar legs (arm/forearm, thigh/shin) on broad round feet with 14 toenails, a short tail
  with a 7-hair tuft; and the fungus: a stout fibrous stalk rising from the spine with a ring on it, a broad domed
  cap with a wavy rolled rim, gills under it, and four small mushrooms sprouting from the shoulders and back.
- **The skin** (shaders/world/mammoth.gdshader): bump-mapped in the shader from each vertex's rest place (CUSTOM0 -
  the detail rides with the bones): thick skin cracked into plates (two scales), folded at the joints and ringed along
  the trunk and neck, mottled, sparse coarse brown hair (more on the hump and head), mud caked up the legs, dust on
  the back, light through the thin ears; worn toenails; ivory tusks with growth lines, stained at the root, polished
  at the tips; small dark glossy eyes; the cap moist and warted (c2), its gills pale radiating plates, the stalk
  fibrous and stained toward its root. Detail fades with distance (no shimmer). Photoreal, no outlines.
- **The motion** (CosmosMammoth.Rig.step): the walk a lateral-sequence four-beat gait (left hind, left fore, right
  hind, right fore, the fore a quarter cycle after its hind), duty 0.68; an amble when it hurries (duty 0.52, never
  fewer than two feet down - no moment off the ground); stride length by speed. Each foot is planted by two-bone IK
  (the elbow bent back, the knee forward), the sole flat in stance; the front wrist folds the sole to the rear in the
  swing. The body rides over its stance legs - it rises and sinks as each leg passes under it (the inverted pendulum
  from the legs' reach), pitches between fore and hind, sways and shifts from side to side, breathes. The head nods
  with the fore feet, the ears fan slowly (a wave rolling out), the trunk swings with the stride, the tail swishes and
  flicks, the cap jiggles on its stalk (a spring on the body's sway and bounce, the cap squashing a little). Standing
  about: grazing (the trunk down to the ground ahead, sweeping, then curling a mouthful up to its mouth; the jaw
  chewing), looking round, fanning its ears, resting a hind leg on its toe (the weight shifted), throwing dust over its
  back; walking slowly it feels over the ground with its trunk. Hurt: it trumpets (the trunk raised, the head up, the
  ears spread); upset: the ears out, the tail up. Posed at most 60 times a second (its motion is slow; ~42 us a pose).
- **Towering and calm** (CosmosFauna.SPECIES "mykelephas"): 130 -> 780 px high (2.4 -> 14 m; ~16 m to the cap's top),
  walk 0.8 -> 2 m/s, run 2 -> 5 m/s (scaled for its size), health 120 -> 600, bite 16 -> 35 (when it charges), a herd,
  a new temper "calm" (CosmosCreature.SIGHT 0: it never runs from you). Shot: it stops, turns to face you and trumpets,
  then strides off heavily (shot again meanwhile, it keeps going); hurt below half its health it charges you for 8 s.
  Its reach 1.1 x its scale (8.7 m: shots, bites); its legs are pillars the walker is kept out of (CosmosCreature.
  push_walker from Cosmos.walker_bumps - you walk between and under it); the camera stops short of its bulk
  (cam_solid + cam_hit: the body and head as ellipsoids); drawn to 480 m (the LODs far off); a herd spawns spread
  2.6 x its scale apart (Cosmos._life); feet planted at its size (all in unit space).
- **CosmosCreature**: the fox's hooks generalised (no new member vars): kind "model" "fox" or "mammoth" -> _fox_build
  through _rigged() (CosmosFox / CosmosMammoth: material, skeleton, skin, rig, mesh); `_rig` untyped; CosmosFox.rig().
- **CosmosWarm**: CosmosMammoth.start() and its skinned mesh with its shader drawn at the title (no compile hitch).
- **The guide** (data/docs/game.md): the mammoths calm, 14 m high, what they do when shot. The space3d_foot shot's
  caption no longer promises mammoths (the woods hide them); doc_shots places big animals further off.

**Numbers:** 6,906 triangles, 4,009 vertices (the generic heavy kit: ~20 primitive parts, several draw calls); LODs
down to 94 triangles; 31 bones; built in ~25-40 ms on a worker; the rig ~42 us a pose at <= 60 poses/s (~10 us a
frame a mammoth at 600 FPS - unthrottled it was 70 us a frame each). Frame rate A/B in my own window (4 mammoths in
view, shadows; the machine shared, noisy): own model 694 / 700 FPS vs the generic kit 591 / 289 FPS - no measurable
cost (one skinned draw call instead of many).

**Files:** scripts/world/life/cosmos_mammoth.gd (new), shaders/world/mammoth.gdshader (new), tests/test_mammoth.gd
(new); scripts/world/life/cosmos_creature.gd, cosmos_fauna.gd, cosmos_fox.gd (rig()); scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd
(herd spacing, walker kept out of mammoth legs); scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd; tests/test_fox.gd (typed rig),
tests/test_cosmos.gd (test_mammoths_calm_and_solid), tests/doc_shots.gd; data/docs/game.md, data/docs/shots.json,
data/docs/shots/space3d_foot.jpg (+ space3d_trader, space3d_port retaken: stale through cosmos.gd).

## 2026-11-28 - Sunrise and sunset on the HUD, markers behind the ground, the compass names what's ahead, a walk that builds to a run
- **Sunrise / sunset** (the user: "under the weather indicators, add a new indicator that shows time to sunrise and
  time to sunset with relevant icons"): a second line under the weather - a half sun on the horizon with an arrow up
  (Sunrise 1h 25m) and one with an arrow down (Sunset 41m). The worlds don't turn: a place's hour moves as its world
  goes round the star, so the times come from the world's own orbit (and its planet's, for a moon) - stepped through
  a year in 72 steps, the crossings narrowed by halving; worked out every 2 s, counted down between
  (CosmosHud.sun_times; "-" for a pole's long day or night).
- **Markers behind the ground** (the user: "i still see markers over the ground"): the line of sight was sampled 20
  times over at most 5 km - 250 m apart, a hill narrower than that missed, anything further never hidden but by the
  world's curve. Now sampled all the way to the marker, 2 m apart near you growing to 5% of the distance (at most
  400 m), to a point 1.5 m over the thing's foot.
- **The compass names what's ahead** (the user: "aligning compass with a marker should display the name of the marker
  and its distance"): a mark within 2.5 degrees of the heading - in space or on foot - its name and distance under
  the heading's readout (the nearer one if two are), in the mark's colour.
- **A walk that builds up to a run** (the user: "when I press forward on foot, the automaton keeps accelerating until
  12 seconds later it starts running and keeps running as long as forward is pressed; if the movement stops it resets
  back to simple walking"): forward held on the ground, the pace rises from the walk (3.4 m/s) to the run (8 m/s) over
  STRIDE_UP 12 s (smoothly), the walk clip turning into the run on the way; kept while forward's held (a hop or bump
  pauses it, doesn't reset it); let go - a walk again. Shift still runs at once.
- Tests: test_sunrise_and_sunset_readout, test_walk_builds_to_a_run, the compass test (facing a station names it).
Files: scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd.

## 2026-11-28 - The worlds turn: days and nights of 16-24 minutes; a Day length setting
- **Asked** (the user): "accelerate the spinning of the planets themselves so a day and a night do not take more than
  12 minutes each" - then: "make the speed of day and night a setting too". Before, the worlds didn't turn at all: a
  place's hour came only from its world going round the star (home's year ~3 h). Orbit periods unchanged.
- **The turn** (CosmosPlanet "Its turning"): every world - rocky, moon, gas and ice giant - turns on its own axis.
  Its node's basis IS the turn: `tilt_basis * Basis(UP, angle)`, angle = phase + 2pi (day clock / day - year clock /
  year) - its solar day (noon to noon) exactly its day length whatever its year (a moon: its world's year). Seen from
  its north (local +Y) it turns anticlockwise: the sun rises in the east, sets in the west. A pure function of the
  seed and Galaxy.time (spin_of: day 16-24 min, tilt 0-20 degrees, the tilt's direction fixed among the stars - its
  seasons over its year, phase); a ringed giant turns round its rings' axis (the rings now lie in its equator, look
  unchanged). A world with towns: its phase such that its first city has the mid-morning sun at galaxy time 0 (a new
  game starts in daylight - before, the towns were put on the day side at load, so they moved between loads).
- **12-minute rule**: the towns are kept within 60 degrees of the equator (CosmosTown.sites / _more_sites); a world's
  day is shortened so that at 60 degrees, midsummer, the day is at most 12 min (share = acos(-tan60 tan tilt)/pi;
  day <= 720 s / share): at 20 degrees of tilt that's 16.7 min, at 10 degrees 20 min - every day still 16-24 min.
  Nearer the poles summer days are longer (polar lands only: no towns there).
- **Numbers**: days 960-1440 s; tilt <= 20 degrees; a 3 km world at a 20-min day: 15.7 m/s at the equator, 0.52 m
  a 30 Hz step, 0.3 degrees of sun a second... the sun's angle 0.006 degrees a step.
- **Carrying what stands on a world** (Cosmos._orbit_tick, 30 Hz as before): each planet's turn this step (its axis,
  the angle) is applied about its centre to every rider within its air: position (turned in double precision, its
  distance from the centre kept: a parked ship drifts < 5 cm an hour of float rounding), basis (quaternion), and its
  world directions (SPIN_VECS: velocity, facing, heading, _aim_flat, _wall, _steep, _aim), the ship's landing ends, the
  camera's smoothing. Out past its air the turn fades to nothing by 35% of its height again + 1.5 km (SPIN_FREE): a
  ship in space isn't dragged round. A town's/dungeon's NPCs (spin_local) keep their own frames. You, your ship and the
  camera are re-assigned to their body every step (never left behind).
- **Frames everywhere** (~150 sites in 25 files): "planet-local" is now the world's own turning frame: to_local /
  to_global for points, dir_local / dir_world for directions - shape queries (height, density, carves, digs, caves,
  dungeons, push_out), the quadtree's camera, rocks, landing spots (the land cache kept planet-local), towns' frames,
  camps, caves' foes and chests, the walker's and the camera's ground, bumps, revive, the save; things laid on a world
  are its children (towns, gates of caves, camps, chests, builds' lamps now too).
- **Lighting**: the star stays put; the ground turns under it. Terrain, water, atmosphere, gas giants, rings: world
  sun (the terrain's slope now compares its normal in the planet's frame; the water's wave normal brought to view space
  through the model's turn); the clouds: the sun in their own frame (spin_sun each step; their dusk glow's eye too).
  The weather's cells, the temperature, the lamp: the local sun (sun_local).
- **HUD/maps**: sunrise/sunset readout rewritten (your spot's elevation over 1.5 days, sampled 72 times, bisected; 2 s
  cache); compass north = the axis, lat/long in the world's frame (fixed to the ground); the planet map's markers,
  the town plan's you/ship.
- **Saves**: "on_planet" stored planet-local (loads back onto the same ground); the spin angle isn't saved - from time
  and the setting.
- **Day length setting** (Settings.day_length, saved under [game]; Settings > Game > Day length): about 8 min / 12 min
  / each world's own (16-24, default) / 40 min / 1 hour / 2 hours / no turning - a multiple of each world's day. The
  spin clock (CosmosPlanet.spin_clock) carries on from where it was when it changes (no jump); reset on New game / Load.
- **Guide**: data/docs/game.md Day and night, Settings.
- **Tests**: tests/test_spin.gd (new: every world's day and tilt, its towns' longest day under 12 min; a world turns
  by its rate; standing still a minute - same spot (< 0.3 m), facing, lat/long; the parked ship and an animal stay
  put; the sun rises and sets, a day = its length, at its city day and night <= 12 min; a new game's morning; the save
  keeps your spot after the world turned; the setting: no jump, half the turn at 2x, none at "no turning");
  test_cosmos converted to the turning frame (orbit test checks the turn; sunrise; compass); test_roads,
  test_underwater (frames); test_digging probes down its bore.
- **Doc shots**: tests/doc_shots.gd holds the worlds still (day_length 0 for its run, not saved) - each shot keeps
  the hour it picks; the town shots turn the town's world to put it in the morning sun (CosmosPlanet.morning_turn, also
  what gives a new game's city its morning). All 3D shots retaken (daylight; the sunset shot still a sunset).
- **Frame rate** (fps_test 3d, back to back with the turning switched off by a temporary flag; the user's game window
  open, numbers noisy +-40%): no consistent cost (e.g. over an ocean world 332/199 off vs 191/248 on; on foot 108 off
  vs 149 on; dogfight 324 vs 357). Loading: the gate jump's 500-800 ms frame is FloraLods._raster on the main thread
  (the vegetation LOD work in progress, not this change).
- **Fixed on the way**: Cosmos._npc_bumps typed a freed trader (a script error after a long time skip).
- **Risks**: hot reload into a running game isn't safe (the planets' bases change under live nodes) - restart. Code
  that still treats `p - planet.global_position` as planet-local would be off by the turn (grep found none left).
  The towns are now where the seed alone puts them (off the poles) - a save made in a town may load you by a
  different spot (it already varied with the load's time of year before).
- **Files**: scripts/world/space/cosmos_planet.gd, cosmos.gd, cosmos_weather_fx.gd, cosmos_deposits.gd,
  cosmos_veins.gd, cosmos_map_mirror.gd, cosmos_bolt.gd, cosmos_voxels.gd, cosmos_npc_ship.gd;
  scripts/world/life/cosmos_town.gd, cosmos_creature.gd, cosmos_npc.gd, cosmos_caravans.gd, cosmos_traveller.gd,
  cosmos_roads.gd, cosmos_loot.gd, cosmos_underwater.gd; scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, cosmos_hud.gd;
  scripts/world/game/cosmos_game.gd, cosmos_sandbox.gd; scripts/world/build/cosmos_builds.gd;
  scripts/ui/pages/planet_map_page.gd; scripts/ui/main_menu.gd; scripts/core/settings.gd; shaders/world/terrain,
  water, clouds .gdshader; tests/test_spin.gd (new), test_cosmos.gd, test_roads.gd, test_underwater.gd,
  doc_shots.gd, fps_tour.gd; data/docs/game.md; doc shots retaken.

## 2026-11-28 - Forests to the horizon: levels of detail for the trees and shrubs

**Asked:** increase the draw distance of trees and vegetation with a dynamic level-of-detail system - from an
extremely low-poly version far away up to the current full detail up close, many levels chosen continuously by
size on screen, no visible popping - so the forests and meadows reach out to the horizon.

**Done (and why):**
- **A chain of meshes per species** (new scripts/world/life/flora_lods.gd - FloraLods.chain, made with the species
  on the design worker): near (every branch and leaf card), mid (clumps fringed with cards), far (coarse clumps),
  low (new: the far mesh's leaves clustered - k-means, 3-6 clusters - into ellipsoids on a five-sided trunk, shaded
  as one crown) and the impostor (new: three upright cards crossed at 60 degrees and one across the crown, 8
  triangles). The impostors' pictures are each far mesh drawn into an atlas on the same worker (a small CPU
  rasteriser: a side view and a top view, 64 px each, colours bled past the edges for the mipmaps) - one 512 x 192
  texture a planet, on the trees' material.
- **Chosen per plant, by its size on screen, in the shader** (flora.gdshaderinc): each plant's distance over its
  size (the larger of its height and most of its spread, x its scale - MultiMesh custom data) gives a continuous
  level through bands at 2, 3.6, 11 and 28 sizes - a big plane tree keeps its leaves further than a small olive;
  each mesh says which levels it draws (its COLOR.a) and folds the rest away (no triangles); next to a band's edge
  both meshes draw, each a complementary dither of the screen's pixels (15% of a band either side), so one melts
  into the next instead of popping. Each plant fades out by its own reach the same way.
- **Reach and density**: every plant within 120 m; further out a share falling as 120 m / distance - a forest stays
  a forest with a fraction of its trees. Trees reach 3.5 km (on the green world that is the horizon: the whole land
  seen from a hill or flying low), shrubs 320 m, crystals/fungi/cacti 900 m; saplings 70 m.
- **Carried down the quadtree** (cosmos_planet.gd; FloraLods.own / inherit / build): every patch from the coarsest
  level whose size covers 3.5 km (level 2 on the ocean world: 1.4 km patches) owns the plants whose reach falls in
  its band (2.6 x its size down to half that) and hands them down - a patch's plants are its parent's on it plus its
  own. A patch and its children therefore draw the same plants wherever both could be seen, and children replace
  their parent only once their plants are built (the trees never blink out when the ground refines). Each patch's
  plants are built on a worker once its ground is in and its parent's are known, set on its own (coarse) ground -
  the trees stand on the ground that's drawn; coarse patches re-filter theirs when a road or building clears ground.
- **Drawing**: each patch draws only its impostors (all species in one MultiMesh, visibility-ranged). Everything
  finer is the **near field** round the camera: per species and level (split by bearing into 8 sectors, so what's
  behind the camera is culled) one MultiMesh of the plants that level can draw now, gathered on a worker from the
  patches drawn - the near and mid levels after 4 m of movement, the far and low ones after 24 m (or when the
  patches change), a margin for the movement meanwhile - and handed over within the frame's budget, unchanged
  buffers not sent again. (The first version - every level a MultiMesh per species per patch - made 11 000 nodes on
  foot and ran at a quarter of the frame rate; the near field keeps it to a few hundred.)
- Shadows: the solid trees' near and mid levels within 50 m (as before: the finest patches' trees). Grass and
  flowers unchanged (the finest patches, their own fade).
- Fixed on the way: the plant workers read PlanetShape's "ground built over" list while the main thread replaced
  it (a crash in the FPS tour) - they now get a snapshot; a planet leaving ends its queued plant tasks and its
  impostor bake at once (its exit waits for them - a 438 ms frame at a gate jump in a first version).
- CosmosWarm: a custom-data MultiMesh of the impostor with the trees' shader. Tests (tests/test_trees.gd): the chain
  per species (contiguous levels, fewer triangles each step, COLOR.a), the impostor atlas (each stand's views drawn,
  leafy colours), the selection (monotonic, continuous at band edges, bigger plants keep detail further, the share
  falling), the handing down (deterministic; every parent plant in exactly one child; reach within the band; built

## 2026-11-28 - Towns: streets and blocks, lamps that light the night; roads into the streets; main roads and causeways; faster on roads; roads on the planet map
Asked: "add to the city lamps and lamp posts that illuminate the city in the same style as the city" - then:
"roads inside the cities as well: blocks separated by streets, each empire's plan; the outside roads join the
streets at a gate; walking and running faster on roads and streets; roads on the planet map (globe and town plan,
under the fog); every city on a main road, every world with towns two cities or more joined by a main road".

**Streets and blocks** (new TownStreets, scripts/world/life/town_streets.gd): a town is street lines across its
square, cut round what stands in their way (palace, shrine, storehouse) and where they cross (nothing drawn twice);
the blocks between them filled with lots - each house's door onto its lot's street. Each empire its own plan:
Minoa (default) a ring of streets round the palace, avenues out of its gates, a street more each way; Athens and
Ionia a regular grid (the temple at a street's end); Sparta few long streets; Mycenae rings round the citadel and
the avenues through them; the Cyclades many narrow lanes (4 m). A village: a main street and its crossings.
Streets are paved boxes (the stone slot's ashlar paving) a little over the square, in the town's one mesh. The
people's spots are along the streets, and a citizen walks to a near spot next (CosmosNpc._next_spot) - they keep to
the streets. Shrine and storehouse moved onto blocks of their own (layout()); the places/plans follow.
City: 22-54 street pieces, 13-23 gates, 24-64 blocks; village: 3-11 pieces, 3-8 gates.

**Lamps** (new TownLamps, scripts/world/life/town_lamps.gd; placed on the town's worker into its merged mesh):
lamp posts every ~19 m along the streets (main streets both sides, others alternating), a pair at every gate, 9 round
the landing field; wall lamps by doors (both sides of the palace's, shrine's and storehouse's; 45% of houses one);
5 oil lamps hung in the palace's colonnade; braziers at the palace's gates, by the altar and before the shrine.
Placed clear of every solid, doorway and people's spot; posts and braziers solid. Each empire's style: Minoa - red
column wider at the top on a plinth with the running-spiral band, black cushion capital, bronze bowl (40%: horns of
consecration on it and an oil lamp hung from a bronze arm); Athens - slim white marble Doric post, meander plinth,
bronze tripod lamp; Sparta - grey limestone pillar on crimson, lambda band, a bronze shield, a fire basket;
Mycenae - cyclopean block, gold bands, rosettes, red column, gold bowl; Ionia - lapis column under gold volutes,
egg-and-dart, a gold lantern; Cyclades - whitewashed pillar, blue bands, a lantern under a blue dome. A new metal
slot (13: the empire's bronze/gold - TownLamps.METAL) and the town flame slot (14) in building.gdshader.
Per city ~180-230 lamps (127-168 posts, 44-57 wall lamps, 5 hung, 8 braziers), per village ~42-67.
Triangles: ~270 a lamp - a city's mesh 190k -> 246k (Minoa), a village's 42k -> 60k; worker time +150-250 ms a city.

**The light by night**: an instance parameter lamp_lit on the town's meshes (TownLamps.night_of: from the town's sun
height - on from ~6 deg above the horizon at dusk, full ~4 deg below), set 4x a second; the flames (building shader
slot 14) sway and flicker in the vertex shader and glow by night, sunk into their bowls by day (dark oil). Real light:
a pool of at most 8 OmniLight3Ds (range 11 m, no shadows, warm), handed from lamp to lamp round the camera, each
fading in/out (24-34 m); further off a soft additive glow on the ground under each lamp (lamp_pool.gdshader, one
mesh a town, hidden by day, fading out near the camera where the real lights are). Indoors, aboard and underground:
no lamp light (no leaks through walls). New materials warmed in CosmosWarm. TownLamps.of(cosmos) is made by
Cosmos._towns_tick (self-healing after a hot reload); towns built before need to be rebuilt (fly away and back).

**Roads into the streets** (CosmosRoads): a road leaves a town by the gate facing the other town, straight out past
its levelled ground, then the path search; its ends go on in along the gate's street (to the ring round the palace or
the village's crossing) - walked by the caravans, not drawn ("drawn" range from gate to gate: no gap, no overlap).
**Main roads**: city to city, 5.6 m wide (tracks 4.4), paved 900 m out of each city (tracks 260). Every city is given a
main road to the nearest city it can reach - over land, else a causeway (the path search may cross sea at a high cost;
at most CosmosTown.CAUSEWAY 420 m, then LONG_CAUSEWAY 1600 m; last a straight causeway), drawn raised 1.1 m over the
water, paved, its sides sloping in. **Two cities a world**: CosmosTown._second_city appends a city (from its own seed;
existing sites unchanged) where no two cities can be joined - on the same land first, then across a strait.
Galaxy-wide (252 inhabited worlds): 177 worlds got a city added; 247 have two cities or more joinable by a main
road; 5 small-island worlds stay single-city (no room for a second within a causeway's reach - their city has its
landing field); 13 of ~560 cities have no main road (7 of them have a track to a village; 6 are alone on islands);
238 roads have a causeway stretch (the longest 1.67 km of water). A world's network: avg 0.56 s, worst 3.2 s (on a
worker). The second city's search (at planet setup, main thread) costs 0-24 ms a world (sampled round the anchor city).
The planet map's worker can make a world's network too (CosmosRoads.store/cached/key_of).

**Faster on roads and streets**: CosmosWalker - on a road or street (CosmosRoads.on_way: a spatial hash of the roads'
stretches, 12 m cells, made with the network on the worker, + the towns' street rectangles; planet-local; looked up
~7x a second) the walk, the run and the stride's build-up x1.35 (ROAD_PACE), eased on and off. The caravans'
travellers walk x1.35 too (always on the road).

**The planet map**: the world's roads on the globe as lines on the ground (simplified with Douglas-Peucker to ~8 m: a
dark casing, the road over it - main roads wider and warmer, tracks thin and pale), only where the ground's been
seen (redrawn as the fog lifts); the network made on a worker when the map opens if it isn't yet. A town's plan: its
streets drawn (main ones lighter) and the roads coming in at its gates.

## 2026-11-28 - Water: a new sea, lakes and rivers with rapids, a deeper sea floor, a better underwater

**Asked:** a better, more detailed water shader; lakes and rivers on the terrain; some rivers with rapids whose
currents make swimming hard; a better underwater (reflection, refraction, sun rays) - realistic but cinematic.
Then (same day): the sea deeper the further out you swim (it was shallow for too long); swimming that builds up like
the run (a slow start to a fast crawl); and a fix - clouds showed over the sea's waves.

**Lakes and rivers** (scripts/world/space/planet_water.gd, new - PlanetWater; PlanetShape.water): made once a world,
on a worker at the planet's setup (its towns known - their ground made dear, the water kept off them), cached a
session. A grid over the sphere (~46 m cells: ~54k on a 3 km world) of the ground's heights; a priority flood from the
coast in (every cell drains to the sea, the basins filled to their brims); each cell's water down its steepest way;
how much drains through each cell. Cells draining > ~0.11 km2 are rivers; basins filled > 1.5 m, 5+ cells, above the
sea are lakes (24 at most, the biggest). Each river traced from its mouth up (the biggest branch on, the others
tributaries), smoothed (Chaikin), meandering (a noise sideways, not at its ends), a point every 8 m; its water
surface stepping down from its spring (the lowest of the ground before it, never rising), wider and deeper
downstream (half width 2.2-15 m, depth 0.65-2.8 m), shallow riffles now and then; its current from its fall
(0.25-4.6 m/s; faster than 2.2 m/s: rapids). Its bed carved into PlanetShape.height (a channel down to its bed, the
banks shelving up to the land - cut back in valleys, raised to just over the water where the land is lower, never out
in a lake or the sea). Lakes keep their basin's own shape: a smooth field from the basin's cells (kernel-weighted,
the shore at 0.5, wandering by a noise) - a bowl under the level, a lip over it round the edge (the surface's edge
hidden under it), the land beyond. Queries any thread: carve, level, flow, wet, covered, crossing, river_at, lake_at
- a hash of the river points and lake cells by 24 m cube-face cells (one key a query). Amnissos: 36 rivers, 16.7 km,
the longest 0.95 km, ~1.1 km of rapids, 24 lakes; made in ~0.9 s on a worker (the world's ground built once it's in).
height(): +1-2 us a call away from water, ~+8-10 us by a river (planet patches on workers).

**Everything round them**: no plants, boulders, dungeons, veins, deposits or building in them or at their edge
(PlanetShape.cleared asks the water); the towns keep off (rivers routed round them, no lake in one); the roads keep
out of lakes and deep river water - a river crossed only where shallow (CosmosRoads.path: closed like the sea, the
crossings between its cells sampled) and, once a world's roads are made, a ford where each crosses (PlanetWater.ford,
on a worker: the river a shallow riffle there - its bed redone near you). Wet banks and pebble-and-silt beds in the
terrain (terrain.gdshader: the patches' UV.y < 0 says how wet). The planet map: rivers as ribbons, lakes as water at
their level.

**The water shader** (shaders/world/water_surface.gdshader + water_waves.gdshaderinc, new; the old water.gdshader kept
for ice sheets and lava): what's under the water seen through it - the screen behind, bent by the waves (not to
what's in front) - and lost into the water's colour with depth (red first: clear in the shallows, turquoise, the
deep's blue); the sky's colours and the sun's glints by Fresnel; a few steps along the depth buffer up the reflected
ray for what stands over it near (the shore, its trees: screen-space reflections, < 260 m); foam at the shores
(depth against the ground), on wind-whipped crests, in white water. The sea: five long directional waves (31-4.6 m)
- moved in the vertices of a near grid round the camera (Gerstner, 420 m, 4.2k vertices, the far sphere leaving it
its middle) - and two scales of drifting ripples; a swimmer rides the same waves (CosmosWaters.wave_height). A lake:
wind ripples, peaty and green. A river (CosmosWaters ribbons: u metres down it, v across, colour speed/rapids/depth/
fade): ripples carried down at its speed, standing waves and streaky white water in its rapids, smooth where slow.
The web: no screen read - blended by depth. It writes depth: the cloud shells behind it hidden (the bug).

**Rapids and currents** (CosmosWalker._water_step): in a river the current pushes you (all of it swimming or diving,
less wading the shallower); wading slows you (more in fast water); in rapids the stroke is worth less - swimming up
them you're carried off (Amnissos's rapids: ~-2.6 m in 3 s flat out upstream; a calm stretch: +3 m and more). White
water spray round you in fast water (data/effects.json water_spray). Lakes: a slow drift. The river nearest you heard
- a murmur, a roar in rapids (sounds/water/river_1, rapids_1 - tools/sfx_water.py, new, synthesised: bubble chirps,
wash, roar, splashes). Walker's water level: the sea's, a lake's or a river's (PlanetShape.water_level).

**Swimming builds up**: forward held, a gentle 1.3 m/s stroke building to a 3.4 m/s crawl over 11 s (Shift: fast at
once), under water 1.4 to 4 m/s; let go and it starts slow again.

**The sea floor**: shallow only near the shore, then shelving down ever steeper (PlanetShape: the depth remapped
0.55x + 0.21x^2, eased to ~5 amp): Amnissos's beaches on average 0.7 / 5.6 / 16 / 30 / 52 / 58 m deep at 0 / 100 /
200 / 300 / 500 / 1000 m out (before: 0.6 / 1.9 / 3.6 / 5.4 / 8.1 / 5.8). The abysses' floors set ~1.1 amp below the deepest of the floor round them (8 samples).

**Underwater** (CosmosUnderwater, underwater_glow.gdshader): in lakes and rivers too (the water you're in: its surface,
its colour - a lake's peaty green, a river's clear); what stands over the water seen through Snell's window, bent by
the ripples (a screen read); ripples at two scales; finer, stronger light shafts (6 steps). The sea's floor life seen
from just above the (now clear) water.

**Frame rate** (fps_test, new water vs the old opaque sea and no lakes/rivers via a temporary switch, alternated
back to back - but on a machine at load 12-44 with other runs going, so the averages swing 3x run to run): GPU time a
frame, new / old - low over the sea 4.4, 2.5 / 2.1, 2.7 ms; over an ocean world 1.7, 3.2 / 1.4, 1.3 ms; under the sea
2.1, 2.2 / 3.6, 2.0 ms (then trimmed: ripples two lookups instead of three, the reflection steps 10 -> 7 and only
where Fresnel shows them, < 200 m). Average fps new / old: low over the sea 13-25 / 19-91, over an ocean world 57-189 /
59-380, on foot 32-120 / 139-170, under the sea 128-263 / 62-357 - mostly script time (the ground's patch builds:
height() a little dearer by the water's lookups, ~13% of their script time in the profile). Needs a quiet-machine
run. Loading: a gate jump froze 2.2 s waiting on the water's worker (a wait on a task not begun runs it on the main
thread) - every water job now has a stop flag checked in its loops (PlanetWater.make, CosmosWaters.build, ford): the
water's waits on leaving a system < 2 ms each (the rest of that frame is the plants' flora task).

Tests: tests/test_water.gd (new): rivers run down to the sea or a lake, beds under banks, wider downstream, lakes;
deterministic; nothing grows in them, towns off them, roads only through fords; the sea floor drops off; rapids
carry you off, calm water doesn't, adrift you're swept down; swimming builds up; the underwater look in a lake.

Under the sea; new shots space3d_river, space3d_underwater_up.

## 2026-11-28 - Landing pads and their traffic: ships come and go at the cities, pilots ashore, rides to other systems

Asked: cities should have landing pads with NPC ships landing and leaving the planet; local pilots get out of the
ships and stay a bit inside, and can be asked for a ride to a local station or another system for a price.

Done (CosmosLandingField, scripts/world/life/cosmos_landing_field.gd - new, a child of Cosmos, attached from
_towns_tick like TownLamps, so a hot reload brings it in):
- **The pads**: beside a city's landing field, on its levelled ground between the town's edge and the flat's rim:
  3-6 a city (3 + seed % 4), 0-1 a village. Big pads two rows each side of the field (a shuttle's length + 4 m
  long - 39 m, Athens 44 m, the Cyclades 48 m - by 27 m wide, the ship's nose out from the town), a courier's
  small one (24 x 24 m) past them; 12 m between the town's edge and a ship's stern for its ramp and a way along
  it; clear of the field's stone, its lamps and its middle (where the local pilot's and a ridden trader's ships
  land). In the empire's look: EmpireKit's material (its paint, a dark iron kerb, the hazard band, an accent line,
  the roundel with its emblem, a chevron at the nose end), lamps (a glowing line round each edge, a lamp in a
  housing at each corner) in the town shader's lamp slot - lit by night with the town's other lamps - and a
  control tower at the field's far end (plinth, shaft with the roundel, glazed cab lit by night, roof, mast and
  an always-lit beacon). One mesh (EmpireKit zones) and one of lamps a town (~1,200 triangles for six pads and
  the tower), built on a worker when the town is built; their boxes added to the town's solids and grid
  (walked on - the deck 0.12 m up - and the camera's obstacles).
- **The traffic**: each pad has rounds of 420 s (its phase from the pad's key); in 72% of them a ship comes:
  a shuttle (55%), a local trader (33%) or a courier (12%) of the town's empire (75%) or another; a small pad's
  always a courier. Schedule = f(galaxy clock, pad): 34 s from the sky down onto the pad (in from 2.6 km out
  and 1.5 km up, slowing over the town, level and straight down the last 90 m, legs out), 150-260 s on it, 26 s
  up and away (straight up 120 m, then climbing out and gone). Far from you it's only those numbers; within
  2.6 km (gone past 3.2 km) the ship's flown (CosmosNpcShip with a `traffic` hook - its flight set by the
  manager from the clock, carried with the turning world). One ship a pad; none comes down on a pad your ship
  is on (that round given up); a ship hired off a pad leaves it free for that round. Ships at once: one a pad
  of the towns near you - 4-5 typically by a city, 6 at most.
- **Hull "shuttle"** (CosmosHull.size_of, DESIGN): the empire's trader design, smaller - 1.6 x 11 m half length
  (35 m long), 1.8 for Athens and 2.0 for the Cyclades (their slimmer designs need it for walkable insides;
  measured: every empire's shuttle has its rooms and a pilot's seat). Couriers fly the fighter hull.
- **Pilots**: when a ship's down near you (its town within 420 m), its pilot - named (People's given and family
  names, from the round's seed) - walks out of its door and down its ramp (ship space: never a jump), then
  through the town (A* over the town's spots: hops along its streets (TownStreets pieces) or clear of its solids;
  through the palace's gateways into its court; out of the town along a street and its edge to the field) to
  where he spends his time: the square, a house's door, the palace's colonnade (or as near as the way goes). When
  the round's time is up he walks back, up the ramp, in at the door, and it lifts off. Saved mid-stay and loaded:
  the same ship on the pad, its pilot ashore where he spends his time (from the clock; only "pads_taken" saved).
- **Rides**: talk to a shuttle's or trader's pilot ashore ("Talk to Alkmene Minyades, pilot of the Minoan
  shuttle"); a courier has no room. He offers this system's stations, a city on each other world, your
  package's place - and other systems: those through the gates and one gate on, with a station (up to 4).
  Prices: in the system as before (25-140 dr by distance); a jump 60 + 150 dr each (210 dr one, 360 dr two). Paid,
  his ship becomes a hired ride waiting on its pad (CosmosNpcShip hire "wait"): he walks back through the town
  (running), up the ramp to his seat (the local pilot's walk), you after him; it waits for him as long as his walk
  needs. To a station or a town: as the local pilot's ride. To another system: out to the gate, through it
  (Cosmos.ride_jump: your ship left behind - ship_at - and you set down on foot in that system's station's port,
  foot_at, under the loading veil). The town's local pilot stays the always-there one, and now flies to other
  systems too (the same offers).
- Event log: "A shuttle of the Minoans lands at Mochlos's field (pad 2)", "... lifts off from ..." (ships near you).
  Scanner (Z): the pads near you marked, free or taken ("Pad 3, Mochlos (a ship on it)").
- Frame rate (machine busy with other windows; back to back, field off / on): walking through a town 137 / 147 and
  129 / 135 fps; loading from the title worst frame 68 / 69 ms, gate jump 745 / 822 ms (the same with it off: the
  machine's load) - no cost to measure.
Tests: tests/test_landing_field.gd (new, 5): a city's pads (counts, on the level ground, apart, clear of the field;
the mesh, walked on, the tower solid, lit by night); a ship lands on its pad and lifts off, its pilot down the ramp

## 2026-11-28 - Plants: detail further out, leaf by leaf; LodKit - levels of detail for every 3D asset

**Asked:** (1) the trees' full-detail and mid levels reaching much further, and the changes between levels
gradual - a soft, continuous blend in the spirit of a cluster level-of-detail system, not a visible swap (wider
blends, a screen-steady blend, more levels, leaf cards dropping out one by one, no flicker going back and forth).
(2) Then the system generalised into one every kind of 3D asset uses: a chain of simpler versions per mesh made
off the main thread, picked by size on screen with no pops; far assets cheaper.

**Done (and why):**
- **Plants - six levels** (flora_lods.gd, flora.gdshaderinc): near, **near thinned** (new), mid, far, low,
  impostor, bands at 2, 3.5, 7, 16 and 34 sizes (before: 2, 3.6, 11, 28 - five levels). The full detail now
  thins out over 2-3.5 sizes instead of ending at 2; mid reaches 7 sizes (was 3.6, x1.9); far 16 (x1.45).
- **Leaf cards drop out one by one**: every leaf card of the near mesh has a random rank (in its UV2.y); over the
  near level the highest-ranked fold away first, card by card, down to the quarter the near-thinned mesh keeps
  (its own index list: only those cards - KEEP 0.25) - at the boundary the two are the same mesh, so nothing
  changes there.
- **The blend between levels: piece by piece, steady on the plant**: no screen-space dither any more - each leaf,
  and each hand-sized patch of crown and bark, has its own threshold (a hash of where it is on the plant), so the
  finer level's leaves and lobes give way one by one to the coarser one's over 40% of a band either side of its
  edge (was 15%, a pixel pattern). The pattern moves with the plant, not with the screen - no shimmer, and the
  same in the shadows. Moving back and forth near an edge flips only the few leaves right at their thresholds - a
  continuous blend has nothing to flicker (the near field's gathering margins keep every mesh that may be needed).
- Fixed: a planet's exit could wait for its plants' design while it ran (now given up part way, between species).
- **LodKit** (new scripts/world/models/lod_kit.gd): `LodKit.later(mesh, [arrays...])` - a builder hands over the
  arrays it made a mesh from; a worker makes the chain (meshoptimizer through ImporterMesh: seams and skin weights
  kept); the mesh's surfaces are swapped for ones carrying it a few a frame (LodKit.pump, from Cosmos; under
  0.6 ms a frame; materials kept), and from then the renderer picks per instance, per frame (shadow passes too)
  the coarsest level whose error stays under a pixel - no visible step. `LodKit.lods(arrays)` for builders already
  on a worker; `LodKit.commit(st)` for SurfaceTools; `LodKit.reach(gi, size)` - a visibility range by size.
  Applied to: the characters (CosmosModels' merged meshes - player, NPCs, citizens, pirates), the town's merged
  meshes (one line in CosmosTown.Builder.mesh), the empires' ship designs (EmpireHulls), your ship's hull
  (MinoanShip), the stations' baked bodies, space rocks and the boulders, ore deposits, space monsters, the fox,
  the dragonfly, the aeromanta, the mushroom mammoth (its own chain now the shared one), loot.
- fps_tour prints the triangles drawn per scenario (RenderingServer: total primitives).

**Numbers:**
- Plant chain (olive): 4254 / 3034 (near thinned, a quarter of the cards) / 1650 / 984 / 130 / 8 triangles.
- Plants back to back (own bench: 24 views on foot, 4 flying low; the worlds held still - the same views each
  run; the machine heavily shared): GPU on foot 6.88 / 8.80 ms vs 6.74 ms before; flying low 4.75 / 6.49 vs
  4.77 ms; triangles drawn on foot 4.19M vs 2.85M (+47%), flying 1.95M vs 1.22M.
- Sweep (a fly-in, 90 frames 1 m apart, frame-to-frame change): the largest local jump between frames 92 vs
  157 before (the biggest pop gone), mean change the same.
- LodKit, whole 3D tour back to back (on / off), triangles drawn: on foot 5.52M / 5.92M; a fight at a pirate camp
  3.63M / 4.64M (-22%); walking through a town 1.06M / 1.73M (-39%); the planet map 1.51M / 1.71M; the town's
  plan 1.53M / 1.75M; in a dungeon 0.14M / 0.40M (-65%); low over the sea 0.63M / 0.82M; in a station's hangar
  0.18M / 0.23M; draw calls the same. (Frame rates from that pair are not comparable: the machine was shared with
  other runs and other work landed between the two.)
- Loading (LodKit on / off): from the title worst frame 63 / 55 ms, a gate jump 276 / 457 ms - the gate jump's
  long frame is not LodKit's (worse without it).

## 2026-11-28 - Bridges where roads cross water

**Asked:** "roads going over water have bad collision and drawing problems; roads over water should use a
bridge-like structure" (the user's playtest on Amnissos near Galatas: the causeway a flat ribbon 1.1 m over the
sea, its edges hanging in jagged teeth to the sea bed, the waves washing over it so it seemed to bob; not solid -
you swam beside it). Then: "the road should not have an up and down motion like the sea waves, it should be a
static and stable surface".

**Done:**
- **Real bridges** (new scripts/world/life/road_bridges.gd, `CosmosRoads.Bridges`), worked out with each world's
  road network on its worker (deterministic): every stretch of road over water - the sea, a lake, a river
  (PlanetShape.water_level; lava worlds' lava too) deeper than 15 cm - is one bridge (wet stretches within 14 points
  merged). Its deck 4.5 m over the sea (the waves reach ~0.7 m), 3.2 m over a river or lake, level with the banks
  over a gorge (up to 16 m), ramping up from the banks at a 7.5% grade and smoothed; never under the ground.
  Each road gets `bridges`: [{i0, i1, h (deck per point), g (ground), wl, half, piers, spans, emp}].
- **Its shape:** a stone deck (the road's width + 0.9 m each side) 0.8 m thick, parapets 1 m high, piers every ~24 m
  where there's room under it (with cutwaters in the water), segmental-to-round arches between them springing just
  over the water, solid abutment walls where it's low over the bank, lamps on every other pier and at both ends
  (TownLamps' posts, lit by night via `lamp_lit`, glows on the deck and the towns' real-light pool lighting the
  nearest - TownLamps._pick now also takes CosmosRoads.lamps_near). **Each empire's look** through the town
  palette (CosmosTown.material - building.gdshader slots): Minoa red timber railings on stone posts and a low kerb,
  horns of consecration over the piers, the running-spiral frieze on the deck's edge; Athens white marble parapets
  and the meander; Sparta grey stone with crimson coping; Mycenae cyclopean stone with gold coping; Ionia pale stone,
  gold coping, egg-and-dart; the Cyclades whitewash with blue. Static geometry: nothing moves but the lamp flames
  (checked: three frames a second apart on the deck - the bridge pixel-identical; only plants, rain and water change).
- **Drawn:** built on the road pieces' workers (one job: the ribbon and the bridge's stone), arrays and a LodKit
  chain made there, the ArrayMesh on the main thread; the bridge a child of its road piece (visibility 1540 m,
  shadows on). The road ribbon laid on the deck (level across, paved to the parapets - road.gdshader: COLOR.g = on a
  bridge, no verge, straight edge) instead of draped on the sea bed.
- **Solid:** a hash of the bridges' stretches per world (16 m cells, planet-local; one dictionary look-up a query):
  CosmosRoads.deck_probe / deck_floor (the walker's floor_at: the deck, a parapet's top, stepped onto from 0.6 m
  below - under it nothing, so you swim under between the piers) / deck_push (walker_bumps: parapets hold you on,
  from outside they're climbable walls; abutments and piers from below) / deck_solid (the camera's clearance, bolts)
  / deck_top (travellers, donkeys, NPCs kept on the deck) / bridge_near (the ship won't land within 14 m: "a bridge
  below - land beside it") / deck_along (the caravans' way). The walker's slope check ignores the bed under a deck.
  The road pace (on_way) applies on bridges too.
- **Planet map:** bridges drawn as a wide pale-stone casing under the road where it crosses water.
- **Live reload:** roads made before bridges existed (a hot reload, the planet map's) get them on a worker
  (CosmosRoads._deck_job) and their pieces are rebuilt.
- Guide: game.md's roads paragraph (the causeway line replaced by bridges), a new shot `space3d_bridge`
  (tests/doc_shots.gd _bridge3d, data/docs/shots.json).

**Numbers:**
- Amnissos (the home ocean world): 6 roads, 12 bridges, 3.64 km of them, the longest 1653 m (67 piers), 147 piers
  in all; every road point over water on a bridge (967 of 967). A Mycenaean world (Nemea): 2 bridges.
- A bridge piece (~190 m of road): ~8,700 triangles + a 2-level LOD chain, made on a worker in ~24 ms.
- Frame rate, the 3D tour back to back (bridges on / off - a shared, loaded machine, both runs well under the
  baseline): on foot 128 / 110 fps, walking through a town 204 / 198, low over the sea 100 / 87, under the sea
  259 / 251 - no measurable cost (noise larger than any difference). Loading: from the title worst frame 57-62 / 67 ms,
  the gate jump's long frame ~500 ms both ways (not the bridges').

## 2026-11-28 - Landed ships solid as they're shaped; walking into any of them
Asked: "I want precise collisions with ships and the ability to walk inside them" - the towns' field shuttles,
traders and couriers, the ports' traders in hangars and on pads (the box of "NPC ships solid" above was too crude:
wings and fins made it solid in open air). Replaces Cosmos._hull_box / _hull_push.
- **CosmosHullGrid** (new, scripts/world/space/cosmos_hull_grid.gd): a hull as a grid of 0.4 m cells (bigger ships'
  grow to stay within 900k cells: a 200 m hauler ~1 m) of the signed distance to its skin, a byte a cell (1/16 of a
  cell, +-8 cells). Made from the hull's triangles (body + glass, ship space): the cells they pass through marked,
  the outside flooded in from the grid's faces, the rest solid; then exact distances (Felzenszwalb's separable
  transform, both ways). One grid a design and size, made on a worker, one at a time (a queue), cached and shared;
  started for landed ships within 500 m of you; stop flag on leaving (finish_tasks, ProcArt). Lookups O(1):
  trilinear distance + gradient; push (a ball held out across the skin's slope, along the ground; under a roof too
  low, out to the nearest open side), top_below (the top under you within a step), ray (sphere-traced).
  Your ship's tail doorway sealed for it (MinoanShip.seal); glass meshes tagged "hull_verts".
- **Walking round it** (Cosmos._hulls_near / _hull_bumps): landed ships within 60 m (and your own landed ship):
  two balls up your body (at 1.15 and 1.5 m: from a step up to the head) held out - stopped at the skin, free under a belly or
  wing over your head, under one too low kept out. Stood on: CosmosWalker.floor_at (and a port's floor) sees a hull's
  top (Cosmos.hull_floor / hull_deck_floor) - jet or drop onto a wing, its back. The camera (camera_clear: any node
  with a grid) and bolts (CosmosBolt: struck on the skin, sparks there, nothing behind hit through it) stopped by it.
  The doorway (CosmosNpcInterior.door / CosmosShip.door_box) cut out of the solid while the ramp's down and the
  insides are in - the same box as the rendered cut; ramp up, shut and solid. Aboard: no hull (its rooms keep you).
  The camera behind you on the ramp kept down in the doorway, not up in the hull. Your ship's leg bumps moved to
  where its legs are.
- **Walking in**: a town field's ship down on its pad with its ramp down is walked into (not only a hired one) and
  back down onto the ground; while you're aboard it waits on its pad (CosmosLandingField "call").
- Numbers: grids - shuttle 44x28x92 .. 59x32x105 cells (0.4-0.8 s on a worker), trader up to 83x43x150 (1-2 s),
  freighter/hauler ~900k cells (3-4.5 s); couriers (fighter hull) 25-40x10-13x61 (~0.1 s). Designs covered: the six
  empires x shuttle / trader / courier (tests), + freighter / hauler / patrol / raider grids. Without insides: couriers'
  skiffs (2.8 m-tall hull - no standing room; solid all round, as their pilots say), and patrols, raiders, warships
  (never land). Frame rate (3d tour, with / without, a shared machine): town 204 / 210 fps, hangar 441 / 425 fps -
  within noise; loading the same with and without (its long frames are elsewhere).
- Tests: tests/test_hull_grid.gd (a box measured; every design's grid shared and deterministic; walker stopped at the
  skin within a cell, in from the box; a low belly kept out, a high one walked under; dropped onto a hauler's back and
  walked along it; camera and bolts; your own ship; each empire's shuttle and trader walked into to the pilot's seat
  and out, the courier shut); test_cosmos.test_npc_ship_hulls_are_solid rewritten.
